newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila urges Beijing to withdraw Spratlys ships.
newsitem.headline: Manila urges Beijing to withdraw Spratlys ships.

text.p: The Philippines has urged China to withdraw the three naval ships it said had been sighted in an area claimed by Manila in the Spratly Islands, officials said on Thursday.
The Department of Foreign Affairs made the demand in a diplomatic note sent to the Chinese embassy on Wednesday, acting Foreign Secretary Tomas Padilla said.

"In order not to harm relations and set back the cooperation slowly developing in the region, the Philippine government therefore calls on the Chinese government to withdraw the three Chinese naval vessels from the vicinity of Kalayaan and Panata islands," Padilla, reading from his note, said to reporters.

The government said earlier this week the military had reported that three Chinese vessels, accompanied by fishing boats, had been spotted near two of the eight islands in the Spratlys occupied by Philippine troops.

Padilla's note said the presence of the vessels in the area violated a code of conduct agreed to by Manila and Beijing which requires both sides not to take any moves in the Spratlys that would disturb the status quo in the contested area.

The Spratlys are a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, reefs and shoals in the South China Sea. China claims the entire area. It is also claimed wholly or in part by Vietnam, Taiwan, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
